transcription_check.scope: Every assigned page377–396 rendered with Poppler and visually inspected.955verse display lines and one bold heading found. Raw defective source preserved; visual/contextual differences documented per ID. Display lineation provisional.

alignment_check.scope: All955source-English pairs read in four consecutive outputs. Row-alignment, lexical and pronoun corrections applied afterward. Same-agent review only, not independent expert review.

notes.manas-2010:p0377:b001:l002: Кылча жанын literally evokes a thread-thin life, retained rather than simplified to life alone.
notes.manas-2010:p0377:b001:l009: Kutubiy is explicitly identified as Oshpur’s son here, continuing the earlier genealogy.
notes.manas-2010:p0377:b001:l010: The leopard refers to the heroic child; the construction Кабыланды тууганда is grammatically awkward and leaves the birth subject uncertain. Source wording is retained.
notes.manas-2010:p0377:b001:l011: Being parted from his father is retained without deciding whether death, separation, or abandonment is intended.
notes.manas-2010:p0377:b001:l013: Dark faith/purification is the narrator’s confessional language, retained as literary source language without endorsement.
notes.manas-2010:p0377:b001:l017: The Forty Chilten are supernatural saintly helpers of the epic. The collective designation and stated number are retained.
notes.manas-2010:p0377:b001:l018: Кутман, bringer of good fortune, motivates the following account of the name Kutubiy; this is the poem’s naming explanation.
notes.manas-2010:p0377:b001:l019: Олуят is interpreted as saints/holy ones, an oral or defective form related to олуя; raw spelling unchanged.
notes.manas-2010:p0377:b001:l022: Мураа is a faithful supporting companion in this context, as in Yudakhin мур/мураа. Кан is rendered khan, not blood.
notes.manas-2010:p0377:b001:l024: Ирегелеш describes adjoining bases/walls, here neighboring households; the image of physical adjacency is retained.
notes.manas-2010:p0377:b001:l026: Ордо чап- refers to the ordo knucklebone game; gathering pieces is a contextual rendering of жыйгандаш, not a military siege.
notes.manas-2010:p0377:b001:l035: Акылга дыйкан, literally a cultivator of wisdom, is rendered rich in wisdom; the praise of resourcefulness is repeated throughout.
notes.manas-2010:p0377:b001:l040: Даңгылдык is provisionally rendered clear understanding, with possible breadth/openness of character also present.
notes.manas-2010:p0377:b001:l041: The comparative Камбылсыган disparages the enemy’s self-regarded resourcefulness. Direct-speech phrasing and reporting syntax remain provisional.
notes.manas-2010:p0378:b001:l004: The shared reading/forecasting of stars is retained without replacing it with a generic friendship metaphor.
notes.manas-2010:p0378:b001:l005: Twelve separate acts of friendship are stated; the number is not reduced to a general lifelong friendship.
notes.manas-2010:p0378:b003:l005: Көк нөкөр at the waist is interpreted through Yudakhin жөкөр, which equates көк жөкөр with көк жеке; жеке II includes a wide leather battle belt. Waist context favors belt rather than boots or a literal companion. Сөгүлүп remains loosened/unfastened. Source form is uncertain.
notes.manas-2010:p0378:b003:l011: The joyful visit to his wife’s kin is the source’s comparison for going to battle; it does not establish a wedding at this point.
notes.manas-2010:p0378:b003:l017: Көрсө көңүл бөлүнүп is a recurrent attention-drawing formula. Its precise subject is not explicit.
notes.manas-2010:p0378:b003:l022: Kutu is the shortened form of Kutubiy, not another character.
notes.manas-2010:p0378:b003:l023: Literal blood-drinking imagery is preserved as bloodlust; no sanitized replacement of the violent epic characterization.
notes.manas-2010:p0378:b003:l027: Döödür is the giant’s name, distinct from Döngö. Source Дөөдүр is retained.
notes.manas-2010:p0379:b001:l017: Rain and hail in the paired bow/gun lines are the epic’s description of volleys; no specific weather-magic act is inferred here.
notes.manas-2010:p0379:b001:l024: Милте is a match/fuse of a firearm. Burning-match firing is retained without inventing a particular gun design.
notes.manas-2010:p0379:b001:l031: The enemy’s stratagems are kept in this source display row; the knowing clause follows in the next row.
notes.manas-2010:p0379:b001:l038: Two men abreast pierced in one thrust is retained as narrated hyperbole.
notes.manas-2010:p0379:b001:l042: Кутубийдин каптоого has an unexpected possessive ending. Context gives to overwhelm Kutubiy; source spelling unchanged.
notes.manas-2010:p0379:b001:l043: Тору ала is normally a bay-piebald color expression, here applied to a pennon. The unusual bay color is retained.
notes.manas-2010:p0379:b001:l048: Кабары literally news/fame, whereas menace follows the intimidating warrior context. A possible damaged каары, wrath, cannot be established; this interpretation remains uncertain.
notes.manas-2010:p0380:b001:l008: The abrupt exhaustion followed by renewed strength does not specify subjects clearly. English leaves strength impersonal rather than assigning both to one combatant.
notes.manas-2010:p0380:b001:l012: The printed strength-suffices phrase is retained despite the preceding strength-fails line; likely shifting combatant viewpoint is not silently harmonized.
notes.manas-2010:p0380:b001:l013: Карыпчы is an arm guard, per Yudakhin/shared working glossary; соот armor is separately retained.
notes.manas-2010:p0380:b001:l014: Канжыга saddle straps are the comparison for shredded armor; no literal conversion of armor into tack is asserted.
notes.manas-2010:p0380:b001:l022: The arm-guard spreading clause remains on this source row. Its governors are named in the next line.
notes.manas-2010:p0380:b001:l023: Калдай is the historical governor rank (Yudakhin), not an untranslated military name here.
notes.manas-2010:p0380:b001:l034: Zholoy occurs inside what is presented as Zholoy’s own speech. The possible shift of speaker or formulaic self-reference is retained, not corrected.
notes.manas-2010:p0380:b001:l036: Iron-rope net bearers are described as a fighting contingent. The precise historic equipment is not established.
notes.manas-2010:p0380:b001:l039: Тегиз канжар колчонум is interpreted contextually as men all armed with daggers; the exact formation or designation remains uncertain.
notes.manas-2010:p0381:b001:l009: Алеңгир describes a destructive/devastating bow in the Kyrgyz explanatory dictionary and Manas encyclopedia. Сыр жебе is a painted/lacquered arrow.
notes.manas-2010:p0381:b001:l014: The cauldron-sized turban and armful-sized belt are retained as epic size imagery.
notes.manas-2010:p0381:b001:l016: Кисе denotes the belt with pouches, not a bare abstract waist.
notes.manas-2010:p0381:b001:l020: Эпсиз usually excessive/ill-fitting; countless stratagems follows the idiomatic excess sense, provisionally.
notes.manas-2010:p0381:b001:l022: Printed Айбалтай is interpreted as айбалта, battle-axe, in the combat clause; final й appears defective or influenced by Baltay. This contextual correction is explicit; raw source unchanged.
notes.manas-2010:p0381:b001:l032: The speaker/narrative focus shifts to Jakyp, named in line35. The English pronoun anticipates that subject.
notes.manas-2010:p0381:b001:l041: Буурсун is the old plough; the virgin-ground image is preserved alongside the marmot-burrow denial.
notes.manas-2010:p0381:b001:l043: Айдай сары is rendered broad yellow for the open plain; the literal moon-like nuance is uncertain and not silently mapped to a place name.
notes.manas-2010:p0381:b001:l046: Seven uninterrupted days are retained, without reconciling the subsequent rapid escape and sleep.
notes.manas-2010:p0382:b001:l004: Two thousand spears striking at once is retained as the exact stated number and epic hyperbole.
notes.manas-2010:p0382:b001:l006: Канжыгалап extends the strap image to streaming blood. The unusual metaphor is retained.
notes.manas-2010:p0382:b001:l008: The two arms are literal limbs here, not two armies; the following paralysis determines the sense.
notes.manas-2010:p0382:b001:l018: Топтуу күнү, crowded/assembled day, is obscure. The provisional literal phrase is retained rather than silently replacing it with a different number of days.
notes.manas-2010:p0382:b001:l019: Ninety wound sites are retained separately from seven in line17; no numerical harmonization.
notes.manas-2010:p0382:b001:l039: The following violence is conditional on capture/surrender, not a completed event.
notes.manas-2010:p0382:b001:l045: Үйүң күйгөн is a curse, may your house burn; it is not reported as an already burned house. Boar/pig abuse is preserved.
notes.manas-2010:p0382:b001:l046: The voice driving out the soul is the narrator’s terror hyperbole.
notes.manas-2010:p0382:b001:l048: Repeated house-burning curse and pig epithet are retained separately.
notes.manas-2010:p0383:b001:l001: Möndü is retained as the named Kalmyk battle-cry. The rest of the line is translated; this is not an untranslated whole-line utterance.
notes.manas-2010:p0383:b001:l008: Жетелеп means leading; no hand-holding is added because the ensuing escape is on horseback.
notes.manas-2010:p0383:b001:l010: Курулган жылдыз болжошу is syntactically unusual. A shared established star-reading follows the friendship context at378; precise ritual meaning remains uncertain.
notes.manas-2010:p0383:b001:l015: Sixty simultaneous troubles is retained numerically as epic expression.
notes.manas-2010:p0383:b001:l017: Жаңжу is read contextually as the governor-general title; Manchu is the paired ethnonym. The compound’s precise grammar remains uncertain.
notes.manas-2010:p0383:b001:l025: Артын кудай бербесе implies God granting a favorable eventual outcome. English retains the minimally supplied outcome rather than a specific rescue mechanism.
notes.manas-2010:p0383:b001:l034: Арам өл- is a foul/unclean death; the religious implication is retained without classifying a specific doctrine.
notes.manas-2010:p0383:b001:l035: The camel that will not move, bursting, is the printed simile. It has not been corrected to a different animal or manner of death.
notes.manas-2010:p0384:b001:l008: Без denotes a gland or sensitive swelling; the sharp reaction simile is retained rather than replaced with a generic startle.
notes.manas-2010:p0384:b001:l012: The reproach is directed at anyone calling Baltay a warrior, as well as at Baltay; the rhetorical question is retained.
notes.manas-2010:p0384:b001:l017: Khangay follows Каңгай as an epic geographical designation, not a verified modern boundary.
notes.manas-2010:p0384:b001:l024: Төлөө is payment/compensation; the rhetorical question asks whether grief pays anything.
notes.manas-2010:p0384:b001:l027: Наалат is an explicit curse; English keeps it as damn it rather than softening to a neutral exclamation.
notes.manas-2010:p0384:b001:l032: Жобо is provisionally interpreted as sorrow/distress, perhaps a damaged жапа-like form; the reading needs lexical review.
notes.manas-2010:p0384:b001:l033: The apparent blessing may be ironic in this rebuke. Its positive literal wording is retained rather than reversed into a curse.
notes.manas-2010:p0384:b001:l037: The belly-ripping comparison with a donkey is preserved as threatened violence.
notes.manas-2010:p0384:b001:l041: Coat-stripping can evoke defeat/spoliation; the coat is retained rather than replacing the line with the inferred consequence.
notes.manas-2010:p0384:b001:l043: Turning horse rumps toward the enemy and a dog-fight suggest a fighting retreat. Exact tactical formation is not invented.
notes.manas-2010:p0384:b001:l046: Тиктөө is rendered stare/look, provisionally; possible oppressive scrutiny or confrontation is not reduced to a modern technical term.
notes.manas-2010:p0385:b001:l010: Бугу чылбыр is a deerskin lead-rope. Опсолоң is unresolved; supple is provisional contextual wording, not a secure lexical identification.
notes.manas-2010:p0385:b001:l014: Үйрөтүп normally training/teaching; driving him is contextual to the flight, possibly reflecting a damaged үйрүтүп. Raw form unchanged.
notes.manas-2010:p0385:b001:l016: Dragging like a fur cap is the source’s simile. Baltay remains mounted in the narrative; English does not assert that his body was dragged on the ground.
notes.manas-2010:p0385:b001:l017: The repeated үйрөтүп is treated as at385:l014; exact form remains uncertain.
notes.manas-2010:p0385:b001:l019: Эбелек is the light windblown tumbleweed image, retained separately from the preceding cap simile.
notes.manas-2010:p0385:b001:l021: Tulpar is retained as the traditional exceptional heroic horse category; no literal wings are added where unstated.
notes.manas-2010:p0385:b001:l024: Саяң is provisionally read as scant/sparse in the tail-and-mane pairing; exact adjective remains uncertain.
notes.manas-2010:p0385:b001:l025: Kulan denotes the wild ass; the hunt comparison is retained.
notes.manas-2010:p0385:b001:l033: Чыбыр with the rugged-ground adjective is rendered stony provisionally; precise soil/terrain term is unresolved.
notes.manas-2010:p0385:b001:l034: Тоңурайган is an unusual printed mountain adjective; towering is contextual. No silent change to a standard form.
notes.manas-2010:p0385:b001:l040: Börü-Koy and It-Ölbös are retained as place names in the itinerary; their literal wolf-sheep/dog-will-not-die components are not inserted into the poem.
notes.manas-2010:p0385:b001:l043: Ээн калган is left free/alone; context favors horses given their head, not a claim that they are riderless.
notes.manas-2010:p0385:b001:l048: Малма is tanning/softening liquor. The leather-treatment detail is retained without specifying unmentioned ingredients.
notes.manas-2010:p0386:b001:l004: The flesh-dividing comparison is retained literally as horse-motion hyperbole. It does not assert dismemberment.
notes.manas-2010:p0386:b001:l006: The second flesh-dividing comparison is preserved independently of the first; no repetition is removed.
notes.manas-2010:p0386:b001:l010: Жолум үй is a small temporary shelter. The impossible hoof size remains the poem’s hyperbole.
notes.manas-2010:p0386:b001:l012: Clear water from the armpits describes sweat through a literal liquid image; no physiological correction.
notes.manas-2010:p0386:b001:l015: Кошкон кара кыяга is obscure in the itinerary. Joining dark steep path is provisional, not a claimed place-name identification.
notes.manas-2010:p0386:b001:l020: The PDF visibly prints Жакып, Jakyp. The surrounding rescue concerns Akbaltay; possible substitution error is left unrepaired in English and raw source.
notes.manas-2010:p0386:b001:l031: The revival images across31–34 are all retained independently, not compressed to thanks.
notes.manas-2010:p0386:b001:l038: The sacrifice formula is an emphatic expression of gratitude in speech, not a newly narrated killing.
notes.manas-2010:p0386:b001:l046: Raising Kutubiy as Noygut khan is a promise here, not a completed enthronement.
notes.manas-2010:p0387:b001:l001: Макшар refers to the final gathering/resurrection; tomorrow is the eschatological future, not a calculated calendar date.
notes.manas-2010:p0387:b001:l014: Супа садык is true dawn, from the traditional Arabic dawn designation; it is not a person.
notes.manas-2010:p0387:b001:l020: Placing grass on the bare tracks is retained from the tracking/pursuit formula; the precise physical practice is not established.
notes.manas-2010:p0387:b001:l022: The repeated yellow-track/grass formula is retained; no omission as redundant.
notes.manas-2010:p0387:b001:l034: The advancing pit is a metaphor for the enemy’s deadly trap; no literal moving earthwork is inferred.
notes.manas-2010:p0387:b001:l036: Boiling brine is the source’s torment image; шор may also evoke misfortune, a nuance preserved in the scene’s context.
notes.manas-2010:p0388:b001:l016: The question about leaving without fighting is retained despite the surrounding report of flight. Its unstated subject is provisional.
notes.manas-2010:p0388:b001:l023: One is supplied contextually from the following absence of Kutubiy; no exact newly counted number is inferred beyond that contrast.
notes.manas-2010:p0388:b001:l024: All the boys safe is retained even though the next line cannot find Kutubiy. This narrative qualification is not harmonized away.
notes.manas-2010:p0388:b001:l031: Bozayban is Jakyp’s horse name here, not a separate gray wild animal.
notes.manas-2010:p0388:b001:l036: Кайыптан evokes the unseen/supernatural; whether it merely means sudden inspiration here is uncertain.
notes.manas-2010:p0388:b001:l041: Өлгөндө көргөн is the late-born-child idiom. Nearly dead preserves the hyperbole without claiming Jakyp literally died before the birth.
notes.manas-2010:p0388:b001:l048: Jakyp calls the Black Kalmyks my people. This possessive is preserved despite Manas’s opposing view.
notes.manas-2010:p0389:b001:l015: Ата is rendered forefather here because Jakyp is alive and the next lines specify grandfather; no new genealogical generation is invented.
notes.manas-2010:p0389:b001:l020: Бапаң is preserved as Bapang, an unresolved destination/name. Heads may denote persons taken away rather than severed heads; English does not settle that ambiguity.
notes.manas-2010:p0389:b001:l023: Эрен denotes unknown distant lands in the2015 Kyrgyz explanatory dictionary, which cites the exact Karalaev parallel Бирөө кетти Эренге. It is translated contextually rather than treated automatically as a proper name.
notes.manas-2010:p0389:b001:l027: Capitalized Күйөр менен Бышардан is interpreted as caring/worrying kinsfolk, through Yudakhin күйөр-бышар. The unusual capitalization does not by itself establish two personal or place names; this contextual reading remains provisional.
notes.manas-2010:p0389:b001:l035: The rearing of a tireless horse is retained as a distinct image, without silently replacing horse with son.
notes.manas-2010:p0389:b001:l039: The object close kin is delayed after the report of sending messages. English preserves the line boundary and completes the sense there.
notes.manas-2010:p0389:b001:l045: May God never show that face is a conventional horror exclamation, not a request to conceal someone’s literal face.
notes.manas-2010:p0390:b001:l003: Түмөн is the epic countless multitude here; no unsupported exact ten-thousand total is introduced.
notes.manas-2010:p0390:b001:l007: Асаба and туу both concern the standard/banner. The stated seven is retained; exact organization of seven units is not inferred.
notes.manas-2010:p0390:b001:l019: Кара курт is the black spider/karakurt image, not literally a worm infestation. The hostile swarm simile is preserved as source rhetoric.
notes.manas-2010:p0390:b001:l030: Аяш ата is the father’s close/sworn friend, a fictive father relationship; it is not a biological second father.
notes.manas-2010:p0390:b001:l038: The witness capitalizes Балтай, which is retained as Baltay striking. A possible балта axe interpretation is not silently substituted.
notes.manas-2010:p0390:b001:l042: Тоз is dust in this earth-and-dust formula, supported by the2015 explanatory dictionary and shared glossary; it is not birch bark here.
notes.manas-2010:p0390:b001:l045: Baltay’s death is Jakyp’s conjecture. It is not verified by the narrator; the preceding escape is retained.
notes.manas-2010:p0391:b001:l008: The beheading is Jakyp’s fearful inference, not an independently narrated death of Kutubiy.
notes.manas-2010:p0391:b001:l010: The printed pause can misleadingly make Akbaltay the speaker. With11–12 it introduces what Manas hears about Akbaltay and Kutu from Jakyp; the English follows that sentence connection.
notes.manas-2010:p0391:b001:l019: Таштуу denotes officials bearing rank stones in this context; the stone insignia are translated rather than leaving a rank word untranslated.
notes.manas-2010:p0391:b001:l024: The plural if we die is retained before the following singular resolutions; no uniform pronoun is imposed.
notes.manas-2010:p0391:b001:l039: Кызыкканын бөлөйүн is a threat to break/disrupt the enemy’s eagerness; the idiom remains provisional.
notes.manas-2010:p0392:b001:l004: Extraction prints чечин while the rendered PDF reads чейин. English translates as far as; raw extraction is preserved with this visual correction recorded.
notes.manas-2010:p0392:b001:l015: The unborn/sinking-away self-curse is retained, without rationalizing the impossible retrospective birth condition.
notes.manas-2010:p0392:b001:l016: The soft-stemmed stalk ripening formula is paired with autumn gossamer. Yudakhin мыйзам cites these exact adjacent lines.
notes.manas-2010:p0392:b001:l017: Мыйзам гүлү means airborne autumn spider gossamer in Yudakhin, not flowers of a law. Exact formula independently checked in the primary dictionary.
notes.manas-2010:p0392:b001:l018: Six months is retained, as are later repetitions of this promise; the seasonal formula is not used to change the number.
notes.manas-2010:p0392:b001:l022: Милек is retained as milek, an uncertain form apparently related to the epic multitude unit ilek. Seven is explicit; no invented decimal size or exact army total is supplied. This is a single unresolved unit within a translated sentence, not an untranslated utterance.
notes.manas-2010:p0392:b001:l032: The contrast not horses but cattle is retained despite the apparent lesser prize. No silent inversion or deletion.
notes.manas-2010:p0392:b001:l041: Кызырдуу evokes Kydyr’s favor/protection, following the established proper-name convention; it is not simply worldly luck.
notes.manas-2010:p0392:b001:l043: Letters from many places are retained literally. The exact kind of letters or grants is not stated.
notes.manas-2010:p0392:b001:l045: Зайыппуруш is an epithet for supremely famous epic heroes in Yudakhin; rendered Supremely Renowned, not transliterated as an unexplained utterance or parsed as wife-related components.
notes.manas-2010:p0393:b001:l005: Кызыр is standardized as Kydyr; visitation/blessing follows the epic religious context.
notes.manas-2010:p0393:b001:l007: Grief at ease and joy at death are the explicit paired heroic characterization, not reversed for modern expectations.
notes.manas-2010:p0393:b001:l010: Ала көөдөн is impulsive/headlong or unguarded; it is retained as impulsive even in surrounding praise.
notes.manas-2010:p0393:b001:l011: Буй кыл- is confound/overwhelm here, as in Yudakhin; the following repetition remains separate.
notes.manas-2010:p0393:b001:l018: The printed dative Жакып байына is preserved as to his father. The surrounding syntax of hearing from and addressing him is awkward; no silent source case correction.
notes.manas-2010:p0393:b001:l020: Ардык is interpreted as exhaustion/weariness. The rare printed form remains provisional.
notes.manas-2010:p0393:b001:l033: Өткөрө жаным is an unusual phrase. Life to spend follows the sacrificial resolve; exact idiom unresolved.
notes.manas-2010:p0393:b001:l040: The unstated battle opponents are the enemy, not the forty households in the preceding line. English avoids a misleading pronoun while preserving the destruction/battle sense.
notes.manas-2010:p0394:b001:l014: Чалкалап literally leaning/throwing oneself back is retained in the fighting posture, not replaced with an invented maneuver.
notes.manas-2010:p0394:b001:l016: Көбүнчө, usually/especially, is odd before if Kutubiy has died. Especially is provisional; the conditional is retained.
notes.manas-2010:p0394:b001:l017: Printed кургунду is read contextually as кыргынды, slaughter. Raw witness remains unchanged; uncertainty is explicit.
notes.manas-2010:p0394:b001:l036: Printed Амызың is read as a damaged намысың, your honor, beside ар dignity. Contextual correction is explicit; raw source unchanged.
notes.manas-2010:p0394:b001:l041: Girls and women are explicitly subject to destruction. English neither omits the victims nor invents a specifically sexual act not stated in this line.
notes.manas-2010:p0394:b001:l047: The PDF visibly names Akbaltay inside the speech rebuking Jakyp. This inconsistent name is retained; a possible witness substitution needs specialist review.
notes.manas-2010:p0394:b001:l048: Extinguished then is Manas’s reproach in speech, not a new narrator-certified death.
notes.manas-2010:p0395:b001:l015: Таза literally pure/clean is provisionally the finest or choice men in the threat; the exact idiom is uncertain.
notes.manas-2010:p0395:b001:l019: Кымбат is costly/precious; costly slaughter preserves this unusual adjective instead of silently reducing it to great slaughter.
notes.manas-2010:p0395:b001:l022: Жазайыл is the jezail firearm. Жаңылып can mean a shot striking here; it is not assumed to mean the bullet missed.
notes.manas-2010:p0395:b001:l037: The capture report continues Jakyp’s uncertain account. English retains the reported-speech framing.
notes.manas-2010:p0395:b001:l041: A horse a shot cannot reach and a coat a spear cannot pierce are retained as epic invulnerability claims.
notes.manas-2010:p0396:b001:l001: Алман is provisionally retained as Alman, a river name. No modern geographical identification is asserted; a defective reading remains possible.
notes.manas-2010:p0396:b001:l005: The more spent/more blazing and more dead/more flourishing paradoxes are retained in separate rows, not normalized into ordinary recovery.
notes.manas-2010:p0396:b001:l009: The blue mane is explicitly on the hero’s back here, supporting literal preservation of the recurring blue-maned epithet.
notes.manas-2010:p0396:b001:l021: The prohibition not hastily migrate scopes the fear-and-haste phrase contextually. Printed үркүп is positive fearing/fleeing; the precise coordination is uncertain.
notes.manas-2010:p0396:b001:l022: The ridge’s waters/swimming image is obscure, possibly a flight/exhaustion formula. Literal wording retained; no concrete river crossing plan is invented.
notes.manas-2010:p0396:b001:l025: The missing overt from ending after Altay is supplied contextually for departure; source remains unchanged.
notes.manas-2010:p0396:b001:l028: Өкүлдөгөн is provisionally entrusted/authorized, referring to the sultan as the people’s representative. Exact participial relation remains uncertain.
notes.manas-2010:p0396:b001:l029: The request to learn his fate before departure is preserved alongside the order to migrate; no chronological reconciliation.
notes.manas-2010:p0396:b001:l043: The six-month resolve repeats the earlier speeches and is retained in full.
